Mercor raises $750M at $20B valuation to take AI agent evaluation to enterprises
by Duncan Riley
Artificial intelligence training data company Mercor.io Corp. today revealed that it has raised $750 million in new funding at a $20 billion valuation.
Mercor provides the human expertise used to train and evaluate AI models, drawing on a network of more than 5 million domain experts. Most of that work so far has been for frontier AI labs. The new funding is aimed at taking it to enterprises in every industry, which Mercor argues need their own way to measure whether an AI agent can be trusted with a job.
Co-Chief Executive Brendan Foody said "every job in the economy" will need its own AI agents and that companies will need a way to train and evaluate them on their own work. Mercor spent the past two years building that infrastructure with the frontier labs. The lab business has grown fast. Foody said in a post on X in July that annualized revenue had passed $2 billion in June.
Adarsh Hiremath, Mercor's other co-chief executive, said a model can score well on a public benchmark and still fail on "the systems, policies and edge cases that define how a specific business runs." For each enterprise customer, Mercor builds a custom benchmark that measures models against that company's own standards. Post-training starts from there.
Part of that post-training runs on software from Deeptune Inc. Mercor bought the New York startup in July , and its team had spent the two years before that recreating hundreds of enterprise applications for AI agents to practice on. The company said the new money will pay for research and evaluation infrastructure, including more of those environments.
Mercor did not name a lead investor for the Series D round, which drew corporate money from Nvidia Corp., Salesforce Inc. and Zoom Communications Inc. Returning investors Benchmark Capital Management Co., Felicis Ventures Management Co. and General Catalyst Group Management also participated. Other investors in the round were Fundomo, G Squared Equity Management LP, Glade Brook Capital Partners, Sapphire Ventures, StepStone Group Inc., XTX Ventures and funds managed by affiliates of Apollo Global Management Inc.
The last round came in October 2025 , when Felicis led a $350 million Series C round that valued Mercor at $10 billion. Foody's blog post on the new round says it included a tender offer for employee shares, and the company has not said how the $750 million splits between that and fresh capital.
Frontier labs have been the main buyers of expert-driven training data so far, according to Jai Das, president, partner and co-founder of Sapphire Ventures. He expects that to change as open models get good enough for enterprises to build on, saying Mercor has built "something hard to replicate" from several years of work with the labs.

45ff4df8cc28ea6bda566a9b569df9fc972c3dbd.text:
AI Governance
Top 5 LLM Governance Platforms for Enterprises in 2026
TL;DR
AI governance splits into two layers: runtime enforcement on live inference traffic, and policy and compliance governance across the model lifecycle. Most enterprises need both.
Gartner projects spending on AI governance platforms will reach $492 million in 2026 and exceed $1 billion by 2030.
Gartner also predicts that by 2030, half of AI agent deployment failures will trace back to insufficient runtime enforcement, which is the layer a gateway occupies.
Bifrost is the runtime enforcement option here: virtual keys, hierarchical budgets, rate limits, model and provider access control, and MCP tool filtering, applied before a request reaches a provider.
IBM watsonx.governance and Credo AI govern at the policy layer and do not enforce on live traffic, so they pair with a gateway rather than replace one.
Enterprise AI usage now spans dozens of teams, hundreds of API keys, and multiple LLM providers, often with no central control over who can call which model, how much they can spend, or what data leaves the network. LLM governance platforms close that gap by enforcing access, budget, and policy controls across every AI request. Bifrost , the open-source AI gateway built in Go by Maxim AI, is the best overall choice for enterprise teams that need to route, govern, and secure mission-critical AI workloads with best-in-class performance, scalability, and reliability. This guide ranks the top 5 LLM governance platforms for 2026 and explains where each one fits in an enterprise AI stack.
What Is an LLM Governance Platform
An LLM governance platform is a control layer that enforces access, cost, security, and compliance policies across an organization's AI usage, so every model call is authenticated, budgeted, logged, and policy-checked from a single place. The platform answers three questions for every request: who is calling, what are they allowed to do, and what did it cost.
Governance spans two distinct layers, and the strongest enterprise stacks cover both:
Runtime governance : request-level enforcement at the point of inference, including identity, model and provider access control, budgets, rate limits, content guardrails, and audit logging. This is where an AI gateway such as Bifrost operates.
Policy and compliance governance : model inventory, risk assessment, regulatory mapping, and audit-ready documentation across the AI lifecycle. This is where governance, risk, and compliance (GRC) platforms operate.
The two layers use overlapping vocabulary for different work, which is the main source of confusion during vendor evaluations. A framework for LLM governance aimed at platform engineers separates them in more detail.
Gartner defines AI governance platforms as tools that help organizations adhere to internal policy, regulations, and industry standards, serving as a central repository for trust, risk, and security controls. For a deeper view of how runtime controls work in practice, the Bifrost governance resource page documents virtual keys, budgets, and access control in detail.
Why LLM Governance Matters for Enterprise Teams in 2026
The cost of ungoverned AI is no longer theoretical, and the spending to contain it is rising fast. According to Gartner , spending on AI governance platforms is projected to reach $492 million in 2026 and exceed $1 billion by 2030 as fragmented AI regulation expands to cover roughly 75% of the world's economies. The same Gartner research found that organizations deploying AI governance platforms are 3.4 times more likely to achieve high effectiveness in AI governance than those that do not.
Runtime enforcement is becoming the deciding factor. Gartner predicts that by 2030, half of AI agent deployment failures will trace back to insufficient runtime enforcement in AI governance platforms. Policy documents and risk registers do not stop a misconfigured agent from spending a month's budget in an afternoon; only enforcement at the request layer does.
For regulated enterprises, governance also has to satisfy external frameworks such as the EU AI Act, the NIST AI Risk Management Framework , and ISO 42001. Bifrost, an open-source AI gateway , addresses the runtime side of these requirements with virtual keys, budgets, audit logs, and guardrails, while GRC platforms handle the documentation and risk-management side.
The 5 Best LLM Governance Platforms for 2026
The platforms below cover the full governance spectrum, from request-level enforcement to enterprise GRC. Bifrost leads the list because it enforces governance at the layer where AI spend and risk actually occur, the request itself, while remaining open source and self-hostable inside the enterprise network.
1. Bifrost
Bifrost is the open-source AI gateway that governs every LLM and MCP call through a single OpenAI-compatible API across 25+ providers and 10,000+ models. Governance is built into the data plane rather than bolted on, so policy is enforced before any request reaches a provider.
Its governance model is anchored on virtual keys , the primary governance entity. Each virtual key encodes a consumer's allowed providers, allowed models, budget, and rate limits, and the real provider API keys never leave the gateway. This is the mechanism that makes per-team cost attribution possible without distributing provider credentials. Core governance capabilities include:
Hierarchical budgets that cascade across customer, team, virtual key, and provider levels, with configurable reset windows from sub-hour rolling counters up to yearly. Daily, weekly, monthly, quarterly, and annual budgets can be calendar-aligned so they reset on the UTC period boundary rather than on a rolling clock, which is what finance teams need for month-end reconciliation. Requests that would breach a budget are rejected before incurring spend.
Token and request rate limits scoped per virtual key, so a runaway coding agent cannot exhaust throughput for the rest of the organization.
Model and provider access control per key, restricting which models a contractor, service, or tenant can reach.
MCP tool filtering that controls which Model Context Protocol tools each virtual key can invoke, extending the same governance model to agentic workflows.
For regulated industries, the Bifrost Enterprise tier adds role-based access control with SSO through Okta, Entra, Keycloak, and Google Workspace via OIDC user provisioning .
Audit logs record administrative activity as HMAC-signed events with configurable retention and archival to S3 or GCS, which is the evidence trail SOC 2 Type II, GDPR, HIPAA, and ISO 27001 reviews ask for. Per-request data lives separately in request logs, and conflating the two is a common source of gaps during an audit.
Guardrails run at the same layer, with three Bifrost-managed checks (prompt guardrails, custom regex, and secrets detection) plus integrations with Presidio, Azure AI Language PII, AWS Bedrock Guardrails, Azure Content Safety, Google Model Armor, CrowdStrike AIDR, Gray Swan, Patronus AI, Check Point's AI Agent Security, and Repello Argus. Rules target either LLM or MCP traffic, so the same policy engine covers tool calls.
Bifrost supports in-VPC, air-gapped, and on-prem deployments, and all of this runs with 11 microseconds of overhead per request at 5,000 requests per second, so governance does not add meaningful latency. Teams running coding agents can govern Claude Code, Codex CLI, and Gemini CLI under the same policy layer, as detailed in the MCP gateway cost-governance breakdown .
Best for: Bifrost is built for enterprises running mission-critical AI workloads that require best-in-class performance, scalability, and reliability. It serves as a centralized AI gateway to route, govern, and secure all AI traffic across models and environments with ultra low latency. Bifrost unifies LLM gateway , MCP gateway , and Agents gateway capabilities into a single platform. Designed for regulated industries and strict enterprise requirements, it supports air-gapped deployments, VPC isolation, and on-prem infrastructure. It provides full control over data, access, and execution, along with robust security, policy enforcement, and governance capabilities.
2. Kong AI Gateway
Kong AI Gateway extends the mature Kong Gateway API management platform to LLM and MCP traffic, which appeals to organizations already standardized on Kong for traditional APIs. Kong AI Gateway governs outgoing prompts through allow and deny lists, token-based AI rate limiting, semantic caching, and AI prompt guards that block injection attempts. Authentication options include OpenID Connect, JWT, and ACLs, and it integrates with AWS Bedrock Guardrails for content safety.
The trade-off is operational footprint: Kong AI Gateway runs as part of the broader Kong Gateway and Konnect ecosystem, so realizing its governance value typically assumes an existing Kong deployment, and its enterprise pricing targets larger organizations.
Best for: teams already running Kong for API management that want to extend the same plugin model and policies to LLM traffic.
3. Cloudflare AI Gateway
Cloudflare AI Gateway is an edge-hosted control plane that sits between an application and its LLM providers, adding caching, rate limiting, request retries, model fallback, and usage analytics with minimal setup. Cloudflare's Guardrails feature applies real-time content moderation to prompts and responses, and DLP profiles can flag or block sensitive data. Core features are available across Cloudflare plans, which lowers the barrier to entry.
The constraints are scope and hosting model. Cloudflare AI Gateway is a managed SaaS at the edge rather than a self-hosted component, so prompt data traverses the vendor's infrastructure. Confirm the current scope of its MCP and agent-traffic coverage against Cloudflare's own documentation before assuming agent-to-tool calls sit inside its governance path. Granular per-consumer budgets and hierarchical cost attribution are less developed than in a dedicated gateway.
Best for: teams that want fast, low-effort observability, caching, and basic rate limiting at the edge without managing infrastructure.
4. IBM watsonx.governance
IBM watsonx.governance is an enterprise AI assurance layer that combines AI-native governance with traditional GRC across hybrid, multi-vendor environments. watsonx.governance governs both generative and machine learning models through three areas: lifecycle governance with model factsheets, risk management for fairness, bias, drift, and LLM quality metrics, and compliance tooling that maps obligations to controls for frameworks like the EU AI Act and NIST.
watsonx.governance operates at the model and policy layer rather than the request layer. The platform documents, monitors, and audits models across their lifecycle, which complements rather than replaces a runtime enforcement gateway, and its depth suits organizations already invested in the IBM watsonx ecosystem.
Best for: large regulated enterprises that need model risk governance, audit trails, and regulatory documentation across a broad AI portfolio.
5. Credo AI
Credo AI is a purpose-built governance, risk, and compliance platform for AI, centered on a Policy Intelligence Engine that translates regulations into actionable controls. Credo AI provides ready-to-deploy policy packs for the EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF, ISO 42001, SOC 2, and HITRUST, along with AI use-case intake, continuous risk assessment, and third-party AI vendor risk management. Credo AI was named in Gartner's 2025 Market Guide for AI Governance Platforms.
Like watsonx.governance, Credo AI governs at the policy and oversight layer. Credo AI covers compliance workflows, evidence generation, and stakeholder accountability, but does not enforce access control or budgets on live inference traffic, so it pairs naturally with a runtime gateway.
Best for: governance and compliance teams that need to operationalize AI regulations and produce audit-ready documentation at scale.
AI Governance Platform Comparison
Two of these five enforce policy on live traffic and three do not, which is the distinction that decides whether a platform can stop a violation or only record it. The table below maps each platform to its governance layer, whether it enforces at the request, whether it covers agent and MCP traffic, and how it deploys. Virtual-key-based governance for LLM and MCP traffic explains the enforcement mechanism in the first row.

How to Choose the Right LLM Governance Platform
Match the platform to the layer where your risk lives. Most enterprises need both runtime enforcement and policy governance, but the runtime layer is where unmanaged spend and access risk accumulate daily, so it is the higher-priority starting point.

Use these criteria to evaluate options:
Enforcement point : does the platform block policy violations on live traffic, or only document and report after the fact? Runtime gateways enforce at the request; GRC platforms govern at the model and policy level.
Access and cost granularity : look for per-consumer identity, hierarchical budgets, and model-level access control. The centralized governance layer in Bifrost models customers, teams, keys, and providers natively.
Agent coverage : with MCP and agentic workflows now in production, confirm whether tool calls are governed, not just chat completions. MCP governance covers what that enforcement looks like in practice.
Deployment control : regulated workloads often require self-hosting, VPC isolation, or air-gapped deployment with no external data egress.
Compliance frameworks : verify support for the EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF, and ISO 42001 relevant to your industry.
For a structured capability matrix, the LLM Gateway Buyer's Guide walks through these criteria in depth, and the AI governance explainer covers the policy-layer vocabulary that GRC vendors use.
Frequently Asked Questions
What is the difference between an AI gateway and an AI GRC platform?
An AI gateway enforces governance on live inference traffic, including identity, model access, budgets, rate limits, and guardrails on every request. An AI GRC platform governs at the policy and model-lifecycle level, handling risk assessment, regulatory mapping, and audit documentation. Enterprises typically run both, with a gateway like Bifrost as the enforcement point.
Do open-source LLM governance platforms meet enterprise compliance needs?
Yes. Open-source gateways can satisfy enterprise requirements when they include access control, audit logging, and compliance support. The freely self-hostable Bifrost build ships virtual keys, budgets, and rate limits at no cost, with RBAC, SSO, signed audit logs of administrative activity, and SOC 2, GDPR, HIPAA, and ISO 27001 support in the enterprise tier.
How do LLM governance platforms control AI costs?
They cap spend before it happens. Hierarchical budgets and per-key rate limits reject requests that would exceed an allocation, rather than letting cost accumulate and reconciling later. In Bifrost, budgets cascade across customer, team, virtual key, and provider, and the gateway returns a structured error when a limit is hit.
Can these platforms govern AI agents and MCP tools?
Coverage varies. Gateways with native Model Context Protocol support, such as Bifrost, govern which tools each virtual key can call and apply the same budgets and access rules to agentic workflows. Edge and GRC-focused platforms generally do not sit in the agent-to-tool path.
What are AI governance tools, and how do they differ from AI governance platforms?
The terms are used interchangeably in the market. In practice, "AI governance tools" often describes point solutions such as a guardrails service, a model registry, or a cost-tracking dashboard, while "platform" implies a consolidated system covering several of those. What matters more than the label is the enforcement point: whether the tool blocks a violating request on live traffic, or documents it afterward.
How does AI governance handle shadow AI?
Shadow AI is ungoverned usage that never routes through the sanctioned gateway: employees using consumer chat apps, browser AI, and coding agents with personal keys. A gateway governs only the traffic pointed at it, so covering shadow AI requires an endpoint layer that routes all AI traffic from company machines through the gateway. Bifrost addresses this through the combined AI Gateway and Bifrost Edge model, currently in alpha.
What does enterprise AI governance require beyond access control?
Access control is the floor. Enterprise programs generally also need spend attribution per team and per customer, content and PII guardrails on both prompts and responses, an audit trail of administrative changes, identity integration through SSO so access follows the directory, and deployment options that keep regulated data inside the network. Coverage of agent and tool traffic is increasingly a requirement rather than an extra.

Programs that buy only the first find that policy exists on paper while a misconfigured agent still spends a quarter's budget in an afternoon, which is the failure mode Gartner's runtime-enforcement prediction describes.

Red Hat accelerates agentic adoption across hybrid environments
by Devony Hof
Enterprise ambitions for artificial intelligence are outpacing the infrastructure and budgets needed to support them. Red Hat AI faces a familiar enterprise challenge: turning ambitious plans for artificial intelligence into production deployments that deliver measurable returns.
Organizations must also decide how to deploy and manage increasingly complex AI workloads across existing infrastructure without letting costs spiral. At Red Hat Summit 2026 in May, Red Hat Inc. outlined its approach to those challenges through expanded platform capabilities, automation and an open-source development process that relies on community contributions.
"I think everybody here loves that because that does lead to sovereignty as well," said Rob Strechay , principal analyst at theCUBE, during the event . "They're actually building on top of open source and enhancing it in a way that provides more value in supporting it, which is key to their success."
This feature is part of SiliconANGLE Media's ongoing coverage of the AWS Financial Services Symposium. (* Disclosure below.)
Red Hat expands support for AI across hybrid cloud environments
Deploying and managing AI workloads across hybrid cloud environments presents new operational challenges for enterprises. Red Hat's answer is Red Hat AI 3.4, an updated version of its enterprise AI platform that supports agentic AI deployments and large-scale inference across hybrid environments.
The company also announced two new managed services : Red Hat AI Inference and Red Hat OpenShift Virtualization Service on IBM Cloud. Red Hat AI Inference is designed to integrate real-time AI inference directly into clients' production workflows, while OpenShift Virtualization enables clients to migrate and run virtual machines at scale. Both services are intended to accelerate hybrid cloud adoption .
"What's really going to drive inference demand exponentially is AI agents," said Joe Fernandes , vice president and general manager of Red Hat AI. "We provide a platform where customers can deploy and manage their AI agents across a hybrid infrastructure environment."
The next piece of Red Hat's agentic strategy comes in the form of Ansible Automation Platform 2.7 , which connects AI-generated insights to governed infrastructure actions. Its self-service automation capabilities allow authorized users in locations such as branch offices and factory floors to manage servers and networks within established controls.
"Customers are now able to use their own data to calculate savings and efficiencies ," said Sathish Balakrishnan , vice president and general manager of Red Hat's Ansible business unit. "Every action, whether it's triggered by humans, an event or an AI agent, passes through the same [access controls], approval gates, audit trails, content signing and credential management."
New services aim to mitigate AI budget concerns
AI budgets are booming: according to theCUBE Research , Analysts project that AI cloud spending could approach $2.5 trillion by 2026, growing at roughly 44% year-over-year. However, that investment does not always return concrete value. Research shows that 50.7% of organizations rely on public AI tools such as ChatGPT and Copilot but only 20.2% report enterprise-wide AI deployments built on a governed framework.
"Most people are token consumers and that is part of the reason they're trying to figure out how do they get to production," Strechay said. "How do they get out of these death-by-pilot situations and become token producers so that they can offset the cost or at least lower the cost so they can get to the [return on AI investment] of those applications? You can use [OpenShift] infrastructure along with things like vLLM and some of the other things in Red Hat AI to get and become efficient in how you produce your tokens."
Part of Red Hat's strategy for helping customers manage sprawling AI budgets is its partnership with Advanced Micro Devices, Inc . Together, AMD and Red Hat are encouraging enterprises to rethink the financials of AI. Rather than opting for the newest, most expensive hardware, clients might have better results if matching compute resources to the workload, according to John Hampton , corporate vice president of global enterprise technical sales at AMD.
"So many of these enterprises just ran out and bought big [graphics processing unit] clusters because they knew they had to solve for AI," he said. "Enterprises are coming to us and saying, 'This is exploding. It's good that we're using AI, but we can't afford this anymore.'"
Red Hat has also joined forces with Intel Corp. to help customers determine which combination of hardware and software best suits their workloads. As enterprises look to reduce inference costs, the companies are emphasizing the value of choosing the right mix of CPUs and GPUs rather than relying on a single approach.
"As we've gone through this with our customers in the industry , we've seen that people often have just assumed, 'I've got a hammer. I need the nail to hit it with,'" said Bill Pearson , vice president of data center and AI at Intel. "Once they take a step back to say, 'Wait a minute. I have these [central processing units] in my data center' or 'I need to figure out how to balance the right number of CPUs with the right number of GPUs to achieve that outcome I'm looking for,' they're actually going to get better results at a better price point for delivering lower-cost tokens."
Red Hat AI partnerships extend from enterprise agents to the edge
Red Hat announced several collaborations at the summit, including Red Hat AI Factory with Nvidia Corp. The partnership includes support for Nvidia's Blackwell architecture and upcoming Vera Rubin platform, as well as participation in Nvidia's OpenShell project for AI agent sandboxing and secure execution.
"Moving AI from corporate experimentation to an industrial engine requires a sovereign, consistent foundation across the hybrid cloud," said Chris Wright , chief technology officer and senior vice president for global engineering at Red Hat, in the announcement . "Through our strategic co-engineering efforts with Nvidia, Red Hat provides the architectural control and open source innovation enterprises need to scale agentic AI with confidence."
Red Hat's other partnership announcements focused on agentic AI and edge computing. Boomi LP, which brands itself as a data activation company, is collaborating with Red Hat on a single, integrated stack for deploying agentic AI at scale . The partnerships with Panasonic Connect and Voyager cover edge computing solutions and space edge micro data centers, respectively.
Red Hat's expanding ecosystem of partnerships reflects the growing range of enterprise applications for agentic AI. The challenge for organizations is determining how those capabilities can address their specific business needs, according to Matt Hicks, president and chief executive officer of Red Hat.
"From the board level down ... you have a feeling of, 'We have to be able to harness what this technology can do,'" said Matt Hicks . "The people that will be the most successful with AI are the people that have the most questions. People that know business, they know their domain. Those are the ones [that] have no barriers to what they can do and change. It's just about getting started."
Red Hat expands sovereign AI capabilities and governance
Sovereign AI has become an increasingly important consideration for enterprises seeking greater control over their data and infrastructure. Gartner Inc. forecasts that the sovereign cloud infrastructure-as-a-service market will grow at a compound annual rate of 36% through 2028.
Red Hat is expanding support for sovereign cloud while allowing customers to keep the infrastructure they already invested in. That includes collaborations with Core42 , which specializes in sovereign-by-design infrastructure, and Sopra Steria , a longstanding European collaborator on sovereign AI initiatives.
Red Hat is also extending its software security capabilities as enterprises adopt agentic AI. Fedora Hummingbird Linux is a container-native operating system designed for agent-first development, with an automated software delivery pipeline . Meanwhile, Red Hat Hardened Images provides a catalog of minimal container images designed to reduce vulnerabilities and strengthen software supply-chain security.
At this point, sovereign AI and governance play an essential role in giving customers choice and control , according to Ashesh Badani , senior vice president and chief product officer of Red Hat.
"Whether an organization is meeting jurisdictional mandates or reclaiming its data from proprietary silos, we are providing the capabilities and platforms to build a more self-determined future," he said in a Red Hat press release .
